newsitem.title: SPAIN: BBV makes headway after share spilt news.
newsitem.headline: BBV makes headway after share spilt news.

text.p: Shares in Banco Bilbao Vizcaya strongly outpaced the market on Monday, supported by news of a share split after weakness in the stock last week, dealers said.
At 0950 GMT BBV was up 250 pesetas, or 2.50 percent, to 10,250 pesetas while the Ibex-35 blue chip index was up 1.55 percent to 6,532.23.

Late Friday, the bank announced an increase in the share nominal charged to reserves, a three-way stock split and a buyback of 1.8 percent of share capital from General Electric Capital Services at 9,850 pesetas per share, with 1.0 percent of shares to be subsequently cancelled.
"The moves are good and should make the shares rise a little more, while the deal with GE is neutral," said Ignacio Rodriguez, a dealer at Benito y Monjardin brokerage.
A trader at Central Hispano Bolsa said the stock was being boosted on Monday by basket trades after some price slippage last week, adding that the stock split was largely discounted.
"People were expecting a share split, although they didn't know how they would do it exactly, but the move obviously supports the shares," the trader said.
